lines.text: The sonnet entered English literature in the early sixteenth
century, adapted from the Italian form pioneered by Petrarch,
and has inspired experimentation ever since. Poets writing in
English have created endless variations on the basic formula of
fourteen lines of rhymed verse in iambic pentameter.
From the Renaissance to the modern era, poets have used the
sonnet form to explore romantic, existential, and political themes
in ways both serious and satiric. Because the sonnet is governed
by strict formal rules, it is sometimes used to playfully illuminate
the tension between constraint and creative freedom.
Readings will include sonnets by Sir Philip Sidney,
William Shakespeare, John Donne, William Wordsworth,
Claude McKay, Gwendolyn Brooks, Edna St. Vincent Millay,
Cathy Park Hong, and Jericho Brown. Students will experiment
with writing their own sonnets and will read them aloud in class.
A final ten-page term paper will be due on May 15.
